_comment: The classes scripts/spec-freeze.py freezes, held here rather than as regular expressions inside the script, so one edit reaches both the freeze check and the rule a writer reads. docs/language-rules.md prints the descriptions inside r55, read out of this file at build time. `pattern` is the expression the script compiles; `description` is the same class in plain words. Changing a pattern changes what is frozen, so a change here re-freezes .spec-freeze/ in the same commit.

literal_classes.description: an anchor citation in square brackets, such as `[INV-141]`, `[E-26]` or `[INV-28 kin]`
a bare range token, such as `T-1..T-7`
a number carrying a unit: px, GB, MB, s, a day count, a percentage, or a ratio such as `4:3`
a backticked path or script token — any backticked span with no whitespace that carries a slash or one of the extensions .py, .sh, .json, .md, .js, .ts, .mjs, .cjs

marker_lines.description: any line outside a table carrying a bare `[target]` or `[default]` token
any H3 heading (`### `) carrying a square bracket

_marker_lines_comment: A structural marker line lives in scenario prose and in headings. A Formal-index table row (a line opening with `|`) only DESCRIBES a rule and may mention `[target]` or `[default]` in passing, so it is excluded; it is compacted, and its numbers and anchors are still frozen by the literal classes above.
